fields.name: title
fields.title: Title
fields.description: Identifier for this loop document. There is one canonical loop — the order in which Coordinator.step() ticks every subsystem each frame.

fields.name: steps
fields.title: Tick steps
fields.description: The load-bearing per-frame update sequence from godot/core/coordinator.gd step(). Order matters: each system reads the just-settled state of the systems above it. The clock ticks first; every gameplay system then pulls the dt channel matching its semantics.

fields.name: order
fields.title: Order
fields.description: 1-based position of this system in step().

fields.name: system
fields.title: System
fields.description: The subsystem ticked at this step (the method called in step()).

fields.name: tickChannel
fields.title: Tick channel
fields.description: Which GameClock dt channel this system advances on. real_dt = unscaled wall clock (UI, camera, VFX). player_dt = real_dt scaled by slow-mo + death crawl. physics_dt = player_dt times the 1.2 game-speed (the world). enemy_dt = physics_dt hard-gated to 0 while the swarm is frozen.

fields.name: note
fields.title: Note
fields.description: Why this system ticks here, and why on this channel.

steps.note: Advance the clock FIRST. Everything downstream reads player_dt / real_dt / enemy_dt from the clock, so they must all see the same already-advanced frame. tick(delta) clamps the raw frame delta to MAX_DELTA and eases the slow-mo factor.
World before actors: terrain / hazards / environmental forces establish this frame's collision + force field, so the player and enemies integrate against this frame's world state, not last frame's.

Order INSIDE is load-bearing: player.tick -> camera_rig.tick_input/transform -> combat.tick. Combat reads the camera's fresh aim ray, so the camera tick is split (input + transform) to avoid a 1-frame stale-aim seam.

Re-applies the camera transform AFTER combat wrote per-shot recoil, so recoil lands on the visible Camera3D the same frame. Real dt because camera smoothing must keep running during freeze / hit-stop / slow-mo.

Waves + audio BEFORE enemies: cues audio and arms the next wave's spawn timers ahead of advancing the swarm, so a spawn/telegraph sound leads the on-screen motion. Run on real dt so timers do not stall during a sim freeze.

Swarm on enemy_dt: returns 0.0 while frozen, so the swarm holds position while player + missiles keep running. Also uploads instance transforms to the GPU, so it runs after wave logic spawned/removed this frame's enemies.
Missiles AFTER the swarm: homing missiles read the swarm's just-updated positions to retarget, so the swarm must have moved first this frame.
Bosses AFTER missiles: a boss can be hit by a missile resolved this frame and react (phase change, retaliation) within the same frame, so it updates after missile motion/impact resolution.
XP / score crystals shimmer and drift on visual timing, independent of sim speed — real dt keeps them lively during a freeze.

Pooled VFX lifetimes (shockwave / wind-slash) are pure visual and run on real dt. Explosions flush LAST, after every other subsystem mutated state — that ordering makes chain-explosion multipliers deterministic within the frame.

A pure display pass AFTER the sim resolved this frame: reads the just-settled player/stat/spree state, ages the feed + floating damage numbers on real dt (UI timing is wall-clock, not sim-scaled). Order-last so the HUD shows this frame's resolved state.
